title: SWITCH: match a list of values

screens.prompt: In D2, translate the code in A2 into the item it names, with Unknown as the fallback.

hints.syntax: =SWITCH(value, match 1, result 1, match 2, result 2, ..., fallback): one value, then pairs.
hints.func-switch: Nothing here is counted or compared by size, only a code matched against a short list.
hints.require-ref: Read the code from A2 rather than typing W-01.
hints.value: A2 is the first code in the list and its pair names Widget, so check every label and the spaces inside them.
hints.error: Text divided by zero leaves #VALUE!, which is the error this formula's broken version returns.

reject.why: the results are swapped, so the first pair names Widget a Gadget
a trailing space makes the result a different piece of text
an IF can hold two outcomes, and this one has the labels the wrong way round
the second code is translated instead of the one in row 2
text divided by zero leaves #VALUE! in the cell
the missing comma leaves the function with a value and no pair

screens.prompt: In D3, turn the tier number in B3 into its name: 1 Bronze, 2 Silver, 3 Gold.

hints.syntax: =SWITCH(B3,1,"Bronze",2,"Silver",3,"Gold","None"): the matches are numbers here, so no quotes.
hints.func-switch: Three tiers are three pairs, which avoids a lookup range for four rows.
hints.require-ref: Match the tier in B3, a number, not the code beside it.
hints.value: B3 holds 3, so the third pair returns Gold.
hints.error: Quoting a match turns the number into text, and the cell answers None without any error at all.

reject.why: the top tier is given the bronze label, so the answer is Bronze
the matches are text while the cell holds a number, so the fallback is returned
a two-outcome IF cannot hold three tiers, and this one is inverted as well
the code column is matched as though it held a tier number, so the fallback answers
text divided by zero leaves #VALUE! in the cell
the missing comma leaves a pair incomplete

docs.explain:
SWITCH takes one value, then pairs of a match and the result to give back. It compares the value with each match in turn and returns the result beside the first exact one. The pairs hold plain values rather than comparisons, so a text "3" and a number 3 are not the same match. That is the usual way the function falls through to its default.

A2 holds W-01, so the first pair in =SWITCH(A2,"W-01","Widget","G-02","Gadget","Unknown") returns Widget. The second screen compares tier 3 in B3 with 1, 2 and 3, and the third pair gives Gold. Quote those matches and the tier misses, so the cell falls back to None.

The last argument is what comes back when no pair matches. Leave it out and an unexpected code returns #N/A in the middle of a column of labels.

errors.text: No pair matched and no default was supplied, which is what a text match against a number produces.
A text result was used in arithmetic, or a pair is missing its result.
SWITCH is absent from the version of Excel in use, or the name is mistyped.

docs.atWork: Translating status codes and cost centres into labels without maintaining a lookup range.
docs.outcome: Translate a short fixed list of codes into labels in one formula.
docs.teaches: SWITCH value/result pairs and the default, plus number-versus-text matching
docs.dataset: Item codes with a numeric tier column

seo.title: SWITCH in Excel: match a list of values
seo.description: SWITCH takes one value, then value and result pairs, and returns the first exact match. A text "3" never matches the number 3, so it quietly falls back.
